claims.text: The intervention consists of laser-remelting every deposited layer immediately after its initial solidification.
The expected effect applies to HEAs processed by laser powder bed fusion.
The expected effect applies under an inert processing atmosphere.
The expected effect applies to HEA component features larger than 1 mm.
Remelting power and scan speed can be optimized to avoid excessive evaporation and keyholing.
In-situ laser remelting reduces microcrack density.
In-situ laser remelting refines the microstructure.
In-situ laser remelting homogenizes the microstructure.
In-situ laser remelting improves layer-to-layer bonding.
The additional remelting step heals pores formed during initial solidification.
The additional remelting step heals microcracks formed during initial solidification.
The additional remelting step reduces residual stresses.
Defect healing, microstructural refinement and homogenization, and reduced residual stress improve dimensional accuracy.
Defect healing, microstructural refinement and homogenization, and reduced residual stress improve mechanical properties.
Relative to LPBF without remelting, in-situ remelting decreases dimensional deviations by at least 20%.
Relative to LPBF without remelting, in-situ remelting reduces porosity and microcrack density by at least 30%.
Relative to LPBF without remelting, in-situ remelting increases yield strength by at least 10%.
Relative to LPBF without remelting, in-situ remelting increases ductility by at least 10%.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires at least 20% dimensional improvement, 30% defect reduction, and 10% increases in yield strength and ductility, whereas the falsification rule uses weaker thresholds of 10%, 10%, and 5%. Results can therefore fail the stated prediction without meeting the stated falsification condition.

The prediction separately requires improvements in both yield strength and ductility, while the falsification rule groups them as 'yield strength or ductility,' leaving it unclear whether improvement in only one property is sufficient.
